name: payor-knowledge-base
description: Multi-source Knowledge Base for the HealthBridge Insurance demo. Covers benefits, claims, prior auth, formulary, and provider network content.

dataSources.description: PDF and Word documents: Summary of Benefits and Coverage (SBC), Evidence of Coverage (EOC), Member Handbooks, and Clinical Coverage Criteria.
Structured Azure AI Search index containing the current drug formulary: tier assignments, quantity limits, step therapy requirements, prior auth flags, and specialty pharmacy designations.
Searchable provider directory index: physician names, specialties, NPI numbers, locations, network participation status, and accepting-new-patients flags.
Real-time query interface to the Fabric lakehouse containing adjudicated claims, member eligibility, and prior authorization records. Returns structured data via natural language query.

metadata.note: Requires member authentication context for PHI queries. In demo mode returns synthetic data only.

dataSources.description: MCP server exposing prior authorization criteria, clinical guidelines, and utilization management policies. Supports tool calls for policy lookup by procedure code, diagnosis code, or service category.

tools.name: get_prior_auth_requirements
tools.description: Returns prior auth requirements for a given procedure code (CPT) or service category

tools.name: get_clinical_coverage_criteria
tools.description: Returns clinical coverage criteria and medical necessity guidelines for a service

notes: Replace <FABRIC_WORKSPACE_ID> with the actual Fabric workspace GUID before deploying.

FABRIC PLACEHOLDER: The 'fabric-data-agent-claims' source requires a Microsoft Fabric workspace with a configured Data Agent named 'healthbridge-claims-agent'. This source is a placeholder pending user configuration — the Knowledge Base will function with the remaining three sources (Blob Storage, AI Search x2, MCP) until the Fabric workspace is provisioned. See data-sources/fabric-data-agent/README.md for setup instructions.
Connection name references must match the connection names registered in your Foundry project.
The MCP server URL assumes local dev mode; update to production endpoint for live demo.
topK values can be tuned per data source override; the root retrieval block sets the default.
